# The Navier–Stokes star-cavity suite {#sec-ds-navier-stokes}

The rung where exactness ends and solver discipline begins. Every suite
before this one carries closed-form labels; here the labels come from a
verified finite-element solver, arrive with **measured error bars**,
and grade continuously in difficulty through the Reynolds number — the
bridge between the exact-label ladder and the industrial chapters that
follow.

## The problem

Star-shaped cavities (the conformal geometry family) hold viscous fluid
driven by a **tangential wall-velocity band** — a generalized
lid-driven cavity whose "lid" is a smooth arc-length window of moving
wall, randomized in position, width, and profile. The flow solves
steady incompressible Navier–Stokes,

$$
(u \cdot \nabla)\,u = -\nabla p + \tfrac{1}{\mathrm{Re}}\,\Delta u,
\qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0,
\qquad u = g \ \text{on } \partial\Omega ,
$$

with $\mathrm{Re}$ a global operator scalar. Labels come from a
Taylor–Hood P2–P1 solver with analytic-Jacobian Newton (MMS-verified at
orders 2.9/1.9), and **every case ships its own certification**:
Newton residual ($\sim 10^{-15}$), momentum balance
($\sim 10^{-14}$), normalized divergence, and — on a deterministic
subset — a finer-mesh re-solve bounding the label-noise floor.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds8-bc-diagram
#| fig-cap: >
#|   One training sample, as posed: the cavity wall colored by its
#|   tangential drive speed (the moving-wall band; the rest is no-slip),
#|   query points inside (with the deliberate near-wall band visible), and
#|   the case's own certification stamped beside it — every label carries
#|   its measured error bars.
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, Normalize

INK, INK2 = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e"
SEQUENTIAL = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "book_seq", ["#f0efec", "#e34948"])
CATALOG = Path("..") / "datasets" / "ns_cavity_star" / "v1"

case = np.load(CATALOG / "case_00000.npz")
params = json.loads(str(case["__params__"]))
pts = case["boundary_points"]
cells = case["boundary_cells"]
speed = np.linalg.norm(case["boundary_velocity"], axis=1)
queries = case["query_points"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 5.6))
norm = Normalize(0, speed.max())
segs = pts[cells]
ax.add_collection(LineCollection(segs, colors=SEQUENTIAL(norm(speed)),
                                 linewidths=3.6, capstyle="round", zorder=3))
ax.plot(queries[:, 0], queries[:, 1], ".", color=INK, ms=3.5)
driven = speed > 0.05 * speed.max()
band_mid = segs[driven].mean(axis=(0, 1))
ax.annotate("moving-wall band\n(tangential drive)", xy=tuple(band_mid),
            xytext=(0.02, 0.97), textcoords="axes fraction", fontsize=10,
            color=INK, va="top",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK2, lw=0.9))
ver = params["verification"]
ax.text(0.98, 0.02,
        "this case's certification:\n"
        f"Newton residual {ver['relative_residual']:.1e}\n"
        f"momentum balance {ver['momentum_balance_error']:.1e}\n"
        f"velocity noise floor {ver['label_noise_floor_velocity']:.1e}\n"
        f"pressure noise floor {ver['label_noise_floor_pressure']:.1e}",
        transform=ax.transAxes, ha="right", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5,
        color=INK2,
        bbox=dict(facecolor="#f4f3ef", edgecolor="#e1e0d9"))
sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap=SEQUENTIAL, norm=norm)
fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, shrink=0.7, label="wall speed $|g|$")
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
ax.grid(False)
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Why this rung

Three things no exact-label suite can provide. **Solver honesty**: the
program's evaluation discipline (fidelity columns, noise-floor-aware
claims) had to survive contact with labels that are themselves
approximate — and the measured floors (velocity $\lesssim 10^{-4}$,
pressure $\lesssim 10^{-3}$ catalog-wide) say precisely how much
headroom remains before a model is fitting solver error. **A continuous
difficulty dial**: Reynolds number grades the physics from
Stokes-like to convection-dominated inside one family. **The bridge**:
this is the same physics class as AirFRANS and DrivAerML
(@sec-airfrans, @sec-drivaerml), posed with the exact-label ladder's
split discipline.

## The gallery

The smooth solutions first — three distinct samples (rows: geometry and
drive pinned per row) marched across the Reynolds range (columns), so
each row shows one flow family stiffening from Stokes-like symmetry to
convection-dominated asymmetry while everything else stays fixed.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds8-gallery
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The dense solution fields: velocity magnitude of the Taylor–Hood
#|   solution, three samples (rows; geometry and drive pinned within each
#|   row — the same case construction as the v1 catalog, re-solved at four
#|   Reynolds numbers) across Re = 10, 50, 150, 300 (columns). The wall
#|   ring is colored by its tangential drive speed. Color is
#|   square-root-scaled in speed (shared scale across every panel): the
#|   thin wall jet at speed ~1 would otherwise hide the cavity-scale
#|   recirculation at speed ~0.1 that fills most of the area. Reading
#|   across a row: the driven arc's wall jet penetrates further and the
#|   recirculation pattern loses its Stokes-flow symmetry as Re grows.
#|   Artifact: `book/data/ns_gallery_fields_2026-07-07.npz`
#|   (studies/ns_gallery_fields.py, h = 0.02, ~21k vertices per solve).
import matplotlib.tri as mtri

DIVERGING = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "book_diverging", ["#2a78d6", "#f0efec", "#e34948"])

GALLERY = np.load(Path("data") / "ns_gallery_fields_2026-07-07.npz")
seeds = GALLERY["geometry_seeds"]
res = GALLERY["reynolds_values"]


from matplotlib.colors import PowerNorm


def smooth_panel(ax, k, show_re=None):
    tri = mtri.Triangulation(
        GALLERY[f"case{k}_points"][:, 0], GALLERY[f"case{k}_points"][:, 1],
        triangles=GALLERY[f"case{k}_triangles"])
    speed = np.linalg.norm(GALLERY[f"case{k}_velocity"], axis=1)
    # sqrt scaling: the wall jet (speed ~ 1, a thin band) would otherwise
    # push the cavity-scale recirculation (speed ~ 0.05-0.2, most of the
    # area) into invisibility on a white-anchored map. The scale is shared
    # by every panel, so cross-panel comparison stays honest; the caption
    # states the scaling.
    ax.tripcolor(tri, speed, shading="gouraud", cmap=SEQUENTIAL,
                 norm=PowerNorm(0.5, vmin=0.0, vmax=1.0), rasterized=True)
    loop = GALLERY[f"case{k}_loop"]
    wall = GALLERY[f"case{k}_wall_speed"]
    closed = np.vstack([loop, loop[:1]])
    segs = np.stack([closed[:-1], closed[1:]], axis=1)
    # Neutral thin outline everywhere; drive-colored overlay where driven.
    # A closed loop of N points yields exactly N segments, so wall (one
    # value per dense boundary point) indexes segs directly.
    ax.add_collection(LineCollection(
        segs, colors="#9a988f", linewidths=0.9, capstyle="round", zorder=3))
    driven = wall > 0.02
    if driven.any():
        ax.add_collection(LineCollection(
            segs[driven],
            colors=SEQUENTIAL(PowerNorm(0.5, vmin=0, vmax=1)(wall[driven])),
            linewidths=2.6, capstyle="round", zorder=4))
    lo_b, hi_b = loop.min(axis=0), loop.max(axis=0)
    mid, half = (lo_b + hi_b) / 2, (hi_b - lo_b).max() / 2 * 1.06
    ax.set_xlim(mid[0] - half, mid[0] + half)
    ax.set_ylim(mid[1] - half, mid[1] + half)
    ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.grid(False)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)
    if show_re is not None:
        ax.set_title(rf"$\mathrm{{Re}} = {show_re:.0f}$",
                     fontsize=9, color=INK)


fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(seeds), len(res), figsize=(9.4, 7.4))
for row in range(len(seeds)):
    for col in range(len(res)):
        smooth_panel(axes[row, col], row * len(res) + col,
                     show_re=res[col] if row == 0 else None)
    axes[row, 0].set_ylabel(f"sample {row + 1}", fontsize=9, color=INK2)
    axes[row, 0].yaxis.set_visible(True)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

What the model actually receives is far sparser: 160 query points per
case (128 interior plus a deliberate near-wall band) against 64
boundary panels. The pair below shows the same case both ways — the
smooth truth and the as-posed sampling — which is the honest way to
present a point-cloud dataset: the cloud is the *supervision*, not the
solution.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds8-asposed
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The same case (sample 1, Re = 10) as the smooth Taylor–Hood solution
#|   (left) and as the dataset actually poses it (right): 160 query points
#|   colored by the same velocity-magnitude scale, wall ring colored by
#|   drive speed. Every accuracy number in this chapter is computed
#|   against point sets like the right panel; every field the model must
#|   implicitly represent looks like the left.
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8.2, 4.0))
smooth_panel(axes[0], 0)
axes[0].set_title("the solution (h = 0.02 solve)", fontsize=9, color=INK)
ax = axes[1]
pts = GALLERY["asposed_points"]
ax.scatter(pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], c=GALLERY["asposed_speed"],
           cmap=SEQUENTIAL, s=26, vmin=0.0, vmax=1.0, edgecolors="none")
loop = GALLERY["case0_loop"]
closed = np.vstack([loop, loop[:1]])
segs = np.stack([closed[:-1], closed[1:]], axis=1)
ax.add_collection(LineCollection(
    segs, colors=SEQUENTIAL(Normalize(0, 1)(GALLERY["case0_wall_speed"])),
    linewidths=2.0, capstyle="round", zorder=3))
lo_b, hi_b = loop.min(axis=0), loop.max(axis=0)
mid, half = (lo_b + hi_b) / 2, (hi_b - lo_b).max() / 2 * 1.06
ax.set_xlim(mid[0] - half, mid[0] + half)
ax.set_ylim(mid[1] - half, mid[1] + half)
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
ax.grid(False)
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)
ax.set_title("as posed: 160 query points", fontsize=9, color=INK)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Measured label quality across the family

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds8-noise
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The label-noise floor, measured per case (finer-mesh re-solves on the
#|   deterministic subset): relative label error vs Reynolds for velocity
#|   and pressure. This is the honesty line of the suite — model errors
#|   below these floors would be fitting solver noise, and every claim in
#|   the benchmark tables lives well above them.
manifest = json.load(open(CATALOG / "manifest.json"))
res, vfl, pfl = [], [], []
for idx in range(0, 1400, 1):
    path = CATALOG / f"case_{idx:05d}.npz"
    if not path.exists():
        continue
    p = json.loads(str(np.load(path)["__params__"]))
    v = p["verification"]
    if v.get("label_noise_floor_velocity", 0) > 0:
        res.append(p["reynolds"])
        vfl.append(v["label_noise_floor_velocity"])
        pfl.append(v["label_noise_floor_pressure"])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 3.6))
ax.loglog(res, vfl, "o", color="#2a78d6", ms=4, label="velocity floor")
ax.loglog(res, pfl, "s", color="#e34948", ms=4, label="pressure floor")
ax.set_xlabel("Reynolds number")
ax.set_ylabel("label-noise floor (relative)")
ax.grid(True, color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### The Reynolds-graded gap, and the confound that resolved it

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds8-regap
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The velocity GAP to the nonlinear reference arm vs Reynolds (joined
#|   v1 + low-Re catalogs, binned; positive = worse than the nonlinear
#|   arm). The plain linear arm's gap grows with Re — but the low-Re band
#|   exposed that most of its Stokes-band gap is PARITY, not
#|   nonlinearity: adding the 0o sector to the linear arm closes the gap
#|   below Re ~ 10 entirely (slightly negative: it edges out the
#|   reference there), while the high-Re growth remains — that part is
#|   the nonlinear read-in's. Two mechanisms, separated by a measured
#|   confound check (iterations 37-38).
gap38 = bie["iteration_38_linear_pseudo_confound"]["joined_gap_vs_re"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 3.9))
styles = {"mt_singpair_linear": ("linear", "#e34948", "o"),
          "mt_singpair_linear_pseudo": ("linear + 0o", "#8352c9", "s"),
          "mt_singpair_nl": ("nonlinear", "#2a78d6", "^"),
          "mt_singpair_nl_pseudo": ("nonlinear + 0o", "#1baf7a", "v")}
for arm, (label, color, marker) in styles.items():
    if arm in gap38:
        ax.semilogx(gap38[arm]["bin_centers"], gap38[arm]["velocity_gap"],
                    marker + "-", color=color, ms=4.5, lw=1.3, label=label)
ax.set_xlabel("Reynolds number (bin center)")
ax.axhline(0.0, color=INK2, lw=1.0, ls=":")
ax.set_ylabel("velocity gap to nonlinear arm "
              "($\\Delta$ relative $L^2$)")
ax.grid(True, color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Variations

### The wide-Reynolds sweep (E1): the curve is U-shaped {#sec-ns-e1}

The suite's headline variation — accuracy versus Reynolds, with the
label-noise floor drawn beside the model error — was pre-registered
as experiment E1 with two predictions. All twelve band-training
reports have landed (three log-banded v2 catalogs generated under
v1's exact verification protocol, plus v1 itself; three seeds per
band, protocol frozen at iteration 17; cluster artifacts
`output/e1_bands/` on HSG, @sec-nb-e1-curve). One prediction was
confirmed and made irrelevant; the other was **refuted**.

```{python}
#| label: fig-e1-reynolds
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Accuracy versus Reynolds number on the steady cavity family. Each
#|   band is an independently trained 3-seed arm under one frozen
#|   protocol; horizontal bars show each band's Reynolds extent (the
#|   re10 and v1 bands genuinely overlap), vertical bars the seed
#|   range. The pre-registered prediction was monotone degradation with
#|   Re; the measured curve is U-SHAPED -- the middle decades are
#|   easiest and BOTH the near-Stokes and advective ends are harder.
#|   The measured label-noise floor (gray) rises 2x across the sweep,
#|   exactly as predicted, and is irrelevant: it sits three orders of
#|   magnitude below the model error everywhere, so the labels never
#|   limit anything. The shaded region is the measured steady-solver
#|   ceiling -- Newton stops converging in practical time somewhere
#|   around Re 4200-5000, which is why the sweep stops where it does.
#|   Provenance: cluster artifacts output/e1_bands/ (HSG); values
#|   transcribed from the notebook verdict entry.
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

### band, Re extent, eval_id 3-seed (median, lo, hi), unseen_Re, floor
bands = [
    ("v2-re1",   (1, 10),     0.312, 0.275, 0.349, 0.344, 0.00020),
    ("v2-re10",  (10, 100),   0.257, 0.239, 0.276, 0.375, 0.00021),
    ("v1",       (10, 200),   0.230, 0.219, 0.239, 0.358, 0.00024),
    ("v2-re100", (100, 1000), 0.348, 0.320, 0.401, 0.369, 0.00038),
]
centers = [np.sqrt(lo * hi) for _, (lo, hi), *_ in bands]
median = np.array([b[2] for b in bands])
lo_err = median - np.array([b[3] for b in bands])
hi_err = np.array([b[4] for b in bands]) - median
unseen = [b[5] for b in bands]
floor = [b[6] for b in bands]

### Split axes: the U-shape lives in a 0.2-0.4 window, the floor three
### decades below.  One shared log-Re axis, two honest y windows.
fig, (ax, ax_floor) = plt.subplots(
    2, 1, figsize=(6.9, 4.6), sharex=True,
    gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [3.1, 1.0], "hspace": 0.12},
)

### The solver ceiling: why the sweep stops.
for axis in (ax, ax_floor):
    axis.axvspan(4200, 20000, color="#e34948", alpha=0.07, lw=0)
ax.text(4550, 0.412, "steady-solver\nceiling (measured)", fontsize=7.5,
        color="#a83a39", va="top")

### Band extents as horizontal bars -- re10 and v1 overlap, honestly shown.
for (label, (lo, hi), med, *_), center in zip(bands, centers):
    ax.plot([lo, hi], [med, med], color="#2a78d6", lw=1.0, alpha=0.45,
            solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=2)

ax.plot(centers, median, "-", color="#2a78d6", lw=1.8, alpha=0.6, zorder=3)
ax.errorbar(centers, median, yerr=[lo_err, hi_err], fmt="o", ms=8,
            color="#2a78d6", ecolor="#2a78d6", elinewidth=1.4, capsize=4,
            mec="white", mew=1.2, zorder=4, label="in-band eval (3 seeds)")
ax.plot(centers, unseen, "s", ms=6.5, mfc="none", mec="#eda100", mew=1.6,
        zorder=4, label="unseen-Re extrapolation")

### Band labels dodge their neighbours: v1 sits almost on top of re10,
### and re100's marker collides with its unseen-Re square.
label_offsets = {"v1": (16, -15), "v2-re10": (-18, 12), "v2-re100": (-34, 6)}
for (label, *_), center, med in zip(bands, centers, median):
    dx, dy = label_offsets.get(label, (0, 14))
    ax.annotate(label, (center, med), textcoords="offset points",
                xytext=(dx, dy), ha="center", fontsize=8, color="#52514e")

### The refutation, stated compactly -- the U itself is now self-evident.
ax.text(1.05, 0.424, "predicted:  monotone degradation with Re\n"
                     "measured:   U-shaped",
        fontsize=8.5, color="#2a5fa8", va="top", ha="left", linespacing=1.5)

ax.set_ylim(0.20, 0.45)
ax.set_ylabel("relative $L^2$\n(combined fields)")
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower center", frameon=False, ncols=2,
          bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.01))

### Lower panel: the floor, on its own decade window.
ax_floor.plot(centers, floor, "-o", color="#898781", lw=1.5, ms=5, zorder=3)
ax_floor.set_ylim(1.2e-4, 9e-4)
ax_floor.set_yscale("log")
ax_floor.set_yticks([2e-4, 4e-4, 8e-4], ["2e-4", "4e-4", "8e-4"])
ax_floor.minorticks_off()
ax_floor.set_ylabel("noise floor")
ax_floor.text(1.15, 5.8e-4,
              "measured label-noise floor: rises 2× as predicted,\n"
              "and sits ~3 orders below the model error — never binding",
              fontsize=7.5, color="#52514e", va="top")

ax_floor.set_xscale("log")
ax_floor.set_xlim(0.8, 12000)
ax_floor.set_xlabel("Reynolds number")
for axis in (ax, ax_floor):
    axis.grid(True, color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
    axis.set_axisbelow(True)
    for spine in ("top", "right"):
        axis.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

| band | Re | eval_id (3-seed) | unseen_Re | noise floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v2-re1 | [1, 10] | 0.312 (0.275–0.349) | 0.344 | 0.00020 |
| v2-re10 | [10, 100] | 0.257 (0.239–0.276) | 0.375 | 0.00021 |
| v1 | [10, 200] | 0.230 (0.219–0.239) | 0.358 | 0.00024 |
| v2-re100 | [100, 1000] | 0.348 (0.320–0.401) | 0.369 | 0.00038 |

: The E1 Reynolds bands. {#tbl-e1-bands}

**Verdict 1 — "the label-noise floor rises with Re": CONFIRMED, and
irrelevant.** The floor does rise, 2× from the near-Stokes band to
the advective one. It also sits three orders of magnitude below the
model error in every band. The honest annotation is *"floor drawn,
nowhere binding"* — the labels are not what limits this suite, and
the measurement's value is that it retires the question.

**Verdict 2 — "accuracy degrades with Re": REFUTED as stated.** The
curve is U-shaped. The middle decades (0.23–0.26) are easiest, and
*both* ends are harder: the near-Stokes band reads 0.312 and the
advective band 0.348. A monotone story would have been the
comfortable one, and it is not what the data says.

The confound is stated before anyone falls in love with a physics
explanation: **the arm and protocol were tuned on v1's
$\mathrm{Re} \in [10, 200]$** — the very middle of the sweep. So the
U may be measuring *fixed-protocol regime sensitivity* rather than
intrinsic task difficulty, and the two are not separable without
per-band protocol re-tuning. That re-tuning is registered, not
commissioned; under the program's no-protocol-tuning rule it would
have to be run as an experiment about the protocol, not as a way to
improve the numbers.

Within-band Reynolds extrapolation penalties (unseen/in-band) come in
at 1.10× (re1), 1.46× (re10), 1.56× (v1), 1.06× (re100). These are
**not** comparable across bands — each band's unseen slice sits at a
different relative distance from its training range — so they are
reported per band with no cross-band claim attached.

::: {.callout-note title="Where the sweep stops, and why that is a result"}
The top band (re1000) is absent, and its absence is physics rather
than infrastructure. Generation reached 450 cases and then a single
unseen-split case drawing $\mathrm{Re} \in [4166, 4667]$ stalled the
Newton solve on all eight retry attempts ("backtracking stalled at
residual $\sim 10^{-3}$"). Every train-band case at
$\mathrm{Re} \le 4000$ solved cleanly. Together with the bracket
probes that measured the ceiling (@sec-nb-re-ceiling-final), the
picture is a **soft band, not a hard wall**: stalls begin around
$\mathrm{Re} \approx 4200$ and thicken toward 5000. That is the
steady cavity family telling us where steady solutions stop being
practically computable — a measured limit of the *benchmark*, which
is worth reporting for exactly the reason the pre-registration said
it would be.

One engineering consequence, recorded because it cost a run: a single
unsolvable case took down the whole worker pool
(`pool.imap_unordered`), so per-case solve failures must be
logged-and-skipped rather than raised. Generation is not fault
tolerant until that lands.
:::

## The full evidence {#sec-part-ns}

Moved from the benchmarks chapter: the suite's founding record — label credential, arms, pre-registered verdicts, and the low-Re band.

The evaluation discipline survives contact with a **real solver**:
Navier–Stokes labels from a certified FEM solve, with measured
label-noise floors reported per case, and the contract story carries
over — the pressure wall becomes a *function of Reynolds number*, graded
exactly as the physics grades the nonlinearity. This part is the
program's current frontier.

### Navier–Stokes: the first solver-labeled viscous suite {#sec-ns-cavity}

**The evaluation discipline survives contact with a real solver, and
the contract story becomes Reynolds-graded.** Every ground truth so far
was either closed-form (harmonic constructions, Bessel series, exact
Euler flows) or, in the FEM catalog, a *linear* solve; this suite's
labels come from a numerical solver on a genuinely **nonlinear** PDE —
steady incompressible Navier–Stokes at moderate Reynolds number,

$$
-\nu\,\Delta u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0,
\qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,
$$

with Dirichlet velocity boundary conditions on the bank's certified
star domains. That changes the *epistemic status of every declared
structure*: on the exact Euler suites, drive-linearity of the velocity
and drive-degree-2 of the pressure were facts of the physics that the
architecture could declare as contracts. For Navier–Stokes the solution
map is analytic in the drive with **all** polynomial orders present —
the Stokes component is drive-linear, each convection correction raises
the degree — so the declared-degree arm becomes an approximation
hypothesis, the linear arm's wall becomes a *function of Reynolds
number* rather than an all-or-nothing barrier, and the labels
themselves carry a noise floor that must be measured and reported.
Suite artifacts: `results/ns_solver_verification_2026-07-05.json`
(solver credential), `results/ns_cavity_star_2026-07-05.json` (dataset
and arms), archive key `iteration_36_navier_stokes`.

**The family** (`ns_cavity_star`, generated by
`datasets/generate_datasets.py`, solved by
`datasets/fem_navier_stokes.py`). Star-deformed disks from the bank's
geometry family carry a smooth, band-limited **tangential** boundary
velocity localized on a boundary arc — a driven lid bent around a
smooth cavity. Tangential-only is the load-bearing choice: the drive
has zero normal flux *pointwise*, so the incompressibility
compatibility condition $\oint u\cdot n\,ds = 0$ holds exactly at the
continuous level by construction, and the small discrete defect of the
interpolated trace (reported per case, typically $10^{-6}$) is absorbed
by the mean-pressure gauge multiplier rather than poisoning the solve.
The profile is a $C^\infty$ bump on a random arc (25–50% of the
perimeter) times a band-limited Fourier modulation, normalized to unit
peak speed — so with unit reference length, $\mathrm{Re} = 1/\nu$
exactly, and the global operator scalar fed to every arm is the PDE
coefficient $\tilde\nu = 1/\mathrm{Re}$ (the screened-suite
convention). Splits: `train`/`eval_id` at $\mathrm{Re} \in [10, 200]$
(log-uniform), `eval_unseen_Re` at $(200, 300]$, `eval_unseen_geometry`
at the bank's 0.45–0.65 deformation range, and
`eval_unseen_drive_profile` with modulation modes 3–5 against the
training 0–2. Targets are the velocity (rank 1) and pressure (rank 0)
at 128 interior queries (wall distance $\ge 0.12$) plus a 32-query
**near-wall bucket** (distance 0.02–0.08) — the boundary-layer
diagnostic, stored with per-query wall distances.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ns-hero
#| fig-cap: >
#|   One production case of ns_cavity_star (geometry seed 3, Re = 200,
#|   production mesh). Left: the tangential drive profile on the
#|   boundary, in normalized arc length -- a smooth bump-windowed
#|   band-limited lid, zero on most of the boundary, unit peak speed.
#|   Middle: velocity magnitude of the Taylor-Hood solution (P2, shown
#|   on the mesh); the driven arc throws a wall jet that rolls into a
#|   cavity-scale recirculation. Right: pressure (P1, zero-mean gauge)
#|   with the stagnation-pressure structure at the arc's ends. This is
#|   the field the models must reconstruct from 64 boundary panels, the
#|   drive, and one scalar.
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.tri as mtri
import numpy as np

hero = np.load(Path("data") / "ns_hero_case_2026-07-05.npz")
loop = hero["loop"]
n_vertices = hero["vertex_pressure"].shape[0]
tri = mtri.Triangulation(
    hero["node_points"][:n_vertices, 0], hero["node_points"][:n_vertices, 1],
    triangles=hero["triangles"],
)
speed = np.linalg.norm(hero["node_velocity"], axis=1)[:n_vertices]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10.2, 3.5),
                         gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.0, 1.15, 1.15]})
ax = axes[0]
ax.plot(hero["arc_fraction"], hero["drive_profile"], color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.4)
ax.axhline(0.0, color="#e1e0d9", lw=1.0, zorder=0)
ax.set_xlabel("normalized arc length $s/L$ [-]")
ax.set_ylabel("tangential drive $g(s)$ [-]")
ax.set_title(f"drive profile (Re = {float(hero['reynolds']):.0f})",
             fontsize=9)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)

ax = axes[1]
im = ax.tripcolor(tri, speed, shading="gouraud", cmap="viridis",
                  rasterized=True)
ax.plot(np.append(loop[:, 0], loop[0, 0]), np.append(loop[:, 1], loop[0, 1]),
        color="#0b0b0b", lw=0.8)
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_axis_off()
ax.set_title("velocity magnitude $|u|$ [-]", fontsize=9)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, pad=0.02)

ax = axes[2]
im = ax.tripcolor(tri, hero["vertex_pressure"],
                  shading="gouraud", cmap="RdBu_r", rasterized=True)
ax.plot(np.append(loop[:, 0], loop[0, 0]), np.append(loop[:, 1], loop[0, 1]),
        color="#0b0b0b", lw=0.8)
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_axis_off()
ax.set_title("pressure $p$ (zero-mean gauge) [-]", fontsize=9)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, pad=0.02)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

#### The label credential {#sec-ns-verification}

A solver-labeled suite is only as good as its labels, and model errors
around $10^{-2}$ demand labels an order better. The solver is a
Taylor–Hood P2–P1 finite-element discretization (inf-sup stable;
velocity $O(h^3)$, pressure $O(h^2)$) with exact-Jacobian Newton, a
Stokes initial guess, backtracking, and a warm-started viscosity
continuation ladder; the pressure gauge is $\int_\Omega p = 0$ via a
scalar Lagrange multiplier; linear solves are direct (MKL PARDISO). Its
credential has four independent legs, all in the verification artifact:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ns-verification
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

results_dir = Path("..") / "results"
ver = json.load(open(results_dir / "ns_solver_verification_2026-07-05.json"))
suite = json.load(open(results_dir / "ns_cavity_star_2026-07-05.json"))

conv = ver["mms_square_convergence"]
star = ver["mms_star_resolutions"]["rows"]
star_by_h = {row["target_h"]: row for row in star}
manifest_ver = suite["dataset"]["verification"]

floor_v = max(
    entry.get("label_noise_floor_velocity_max", 0.0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
floor_p = max(
    entry.get("label_noise_floor_pressure_max", 0.0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
mom_max = max(
    entry.get("momentum_balance_error_max", 0.0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
flux_max = max(
    entry.get("boundary_flux_max_abs", 0.0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
rej = sum(
    entry.get("rejected_attempts_total", 0)
    for name, entry in manifest_ver.items() if isinstance(entry, dict)
)
n_cases = suite["dataset"]["n_cases"]

rows = [
    ("MMS convergence order (unit square)",
     "velocity ~3, pressure ~2",
     f"{conv['velocity_order']:.2f} / {conv['pressure_order']:.2f}"),
    ("MMS velocity rel-L2, star, production $h{=}0.0105$",
     "$\\le 10^{-6}$",
     f"{star_by_h[0.0105]['velocity_rel_l2']:.1e} "
     f"({star_by_h[0.0105]['seconds']:.0f} s/solve)"),
    ("MMS velocity rel-L2, star, first-pass $h{=}0.02$",
     "context (see text)",
     f"{star_by_h[0.02]['velocity_rel_l2']:.1e} "
     f"({star_by_h[0.02]['seconds']:.0f} s/solve)"),
    ("label noise floor, velocity (vs $h/1.5$, worst split)",
     "$\\le 10^{-3}$", f"{floor_v:.1e}"),
    ("label noise floor, pressure (vs $h/1.5$, worst split)",
     "$\\le 10^{-3}$", f"{floor_p:.1e}"),
    ("momentum-balance assembly identity (worst case)",
     "roundoff", f"{mom_max:.1e}"),
    ("discrete boundary flux $|\\oint u_h\\cdot n|$ (worst case)",
     "small, reported", f"{flux_max:.1e}"),
    ("rejected-and-resampled Newton attempts across the catalog",
     "reported", f"{rej} (over {n_cases} cases)"),
]
print("| check | bar | measured |")
print("|---|---|---|")
for name, bar, measured in rows:
    print(f"| {name} | {bar} | {measured} |")
print()
print(": The suite's label credential: manufactured-solutions accuracy "
"and order, the finer-mesh label-noise floor, and the discrete balance "
"certificates, all from checked-in artifacts. {#tbl-ns-verification}")
```

One resolution decision is worth stating plainly, because it was
*revised by a measurement*. The first-pass plan ran production at
$h = 0.02$ — velocity labels two orders under the $10^{-3}$ floor
target, the $10^{-6}$ MMS bar demonstrated separately at $h = 0.01$ —
on the estimate that the $O(h^2)$ pressure floor would land near
$8\times10^{-4}$. The generated catalog measured it at
$2.6$–$3.2\times10^{-3}$ across splits: **the pressure is the binding
field, and the first-pass resolution broke the target.** Generation
had come in far under budget (19.6 minutes for 1,400 cases on 26
workers), so the catalog was regenerated at $h = 0.0105$ (2.7 hours on
20 workers; the finer meshes cost the PARDISO factorizations ~8×) —
where the measured finer-mesh pressure floor comes back under
$10^{-3}$ on four of five splits (worst $8.7\times10^{-4}$ on train;
the unseen-drive split's worst sampled case reads $1.26\times10^{-3}$,
26% over target, reported as-is), the velocity floor sits at
$\le 5.8\times10^{-5}$ everywhere, *and* the MMS velocity bar of
$10^{-6}$ is met at production resolution outright
(@tbl-ns-verification), dissolving the two-resolution compromise. The
Newton robustness grid behind the declared Reynolds band — train
$[10, 200]$, unseen-Re $(200, 300]$ — converges in 4–8 iterations
with occasional backtracking on train-band *and* 0.65-deformation
stars up through Re 400.

#### Arms, and what the nonlinearity does to them {#sec-ns-arms}

The comparison reuses the iteration-32/35 configuration exactly (one
head, ranks 48/16, singpair dictionary; 15 epochs over the fixed
catalog, 3 seeds, iteration-17 protocol): the declared-degree flagship
`mt_singpair_q2_pseudo`, the unbounded nonlinear control
`mt_singpair_nl_pseudo`, the pre-registered wall control
`mt_singpair_linear`, the parameter-free `boundary_mean` floor, and the
in-tree Transolver at matched capacity on the same token contract
(coordinates, normals, measures, the rank-1 drive, and $\tilde\nu$ as a
constant channel).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ns-arms
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

suite = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" /
                       "ns_cavity_star_2026-07-05.json"))
arms = suite["arms"]
order = ["mt_singpair_q2_pseudo", "mt_singpair_nl_pseudo",
         "mt_singpair_linear", "transolver_intree_matched",
         "boundary_mean"]
labels = {
    "mt_singpair_q2_pseudo": "MT q2 + pseudo (declared degree 2)",
    "mt_singpair_nl_pseudo": "MT nonlinear + pseudo",
    "mt_singpair_linear": "MT linear (wall control)",
    "transolver_intree_matched": "Transolver (in-tree, matched)",
    "boundary_mean": "boundary mean (floor)",
}
splits = ["eval_id", "eval_unseen_Re", "eval_unseen_geometry",
          "eval_unseen_drive_profile"]
headers = ["arm", "params"] + [s.replace("eval_", "").replace("_", "-")
                               for s in splits] + ["momentum res. (ID)"]
print("| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |")
print("|" + "---|" * len(headers))
for arm in order:
    row = [labels[arm], f"{arms[arm]['parameters']:,}"]

print(": Combined (concatenated velocity+pressure) relative $L^2$, "
"mean ± sd over 3 seeds, per evaluation split -- 15 epochs on the "

"iteration-36 runs predate the driver's strong-form fidelity block "
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-ns-wall
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The pre-registered Re-dependent wall, measured. Per-case relative
#|   L2 pooled over eval_id + eval_unseen_Re (3 seeds), binned by case
#|   Reynolds number (log bins), for velocity (left) and pressure
#|   (right). The PRESSURE gap between the linear arm and the nonlinear
#|   arms grows 4.2x across the band -- the predicted graded wall. The
#|   VELOCITY gap is flat (~0.19 at every Re): the pre-registered
#|   near-Stokes prediction for the low-Re end did not hold (see text).
#|   How to read this: the gap, not the absolute level, is the wall;
#|   all arms share dataset, protocol, and seeds.
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

suite = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" /
                       "ns_cavity_star_2026-07-05.json"))
wall = suite["re_wall"]["per_arm"]
style = {
    "mt_singpair_linear": ("#e34948", "o-", "linear arm"),
    "mt_singpair_nl_pseudo": ("#1a6feb", "^-", "nonlinear + pseudo"),
    "mt_singpair_q2_pseudo": ("#1baf7a", "s-", "q2 + pseudo"),
    "transolver_intree_matched": ("#52514e", "d-", "Transolver"),
}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.6, 3.8), sharex=True)
for ax, field in zip(axes, ("velocity", "pressure")):
    for arm, (color, marker, label) in style.items():
        entry = wall[arm]
        ax.loglog(entry["bin_centers"], entry[field], marker, ms=4,
                  lw=1.3, color=color, label=label)

    ax.loglog(floor["bin_centers"], floor[field], ":", lw=1.2,
              color="#0b0b0b", label="boundary-mean floor")
```

#### Pre-registered versus measured {#sec-ns-verdicts}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ns-ledger
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

suite = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" /
                       "ns_cavity_star_2026-07-05.json"))
v = suite["verdicts"]
p1 = v["P1_linear_wall_grows_with_Re"]
p2 = v["P2_declared_degree_approximation"]
p3 = v["P3_boundary_mean_pressure_floor"]

vel_ratio = p1["velocity_gap_ratio_top_over_bottom"]
prs_ratio = p1["pressure_gap_ratio_top_over_bottom"]
p1_pass = (max(vel_ratio, prs_ratio) >= 3.0)
p1_verdict = "**supported**" if p1_pass else "**not supported**"
p2_verdict = ("degree-2 truncation suffices at these Re"
              if p2["within_2x_seed_sd"]
              else "higher orders matter (q2 trails nl beyond 2x seed sd)")
p3_verdict = "**exact**" if p3["exactly_one"] else "**violated**"

rows = [
    ("P1: linear wall grows with Re "
     "(gap ratio top/bottom Re bin $\\ge 3$, either field)",
     f"velocity {vel_ratio:.1f}x "
     f"(gap {p1['velocity_gap_bottom_bin']:.3f} to "
     f"{p1['velocity_gap_top_bin']:.3f}); "
     f"pressure {prs_ratio:.1f}x "
     f"(gap {p1['pressure_gap_bottom_bin']:.3f} to "
     f"{p1['pressure_gap_top_bin']:.3f})",
     p1_verdict),
    ("P2: declared degree 2 as approximation "
     "(q2 within 2x seed sd of nl on eval_id)",
     f"q2 {p2['q2_eval_id_combined']['mean']:.3f} ± "
     f"{p2['q2_eval_id_combined']['sd']:.3f} vs "
     f"nl {p2['nl_eval_id_combined']['mean']:.3f} ± "
     f"{p2['nl_eval_id_combined']['sd']:.3f}",
     p2_verdict),
    ("P3: boundary-mean pressure floor exactly 1.0",
     f"{p3['boundary_mean_pressure_eval_id']['mean']:.6f}",
     p3_verdict),
]
print("| pre-registered rule | measured | verdict |")
print("|---|---|---|")
for rule, measured, verdict in rows:
    print(f"| {rule} | {measured} | {verdict} |")
print()
print(": The iteration's pre-registered ledger (rules logged in the lab "
"notebook and the driver docstrings before the first training run; "
"numbers from the checked-in artifact). {#tbl-ns-ledger}")
```

**The anomaly, stated plainly.** P1's deciding measurement split: the
pressure leg passed decisively (gap ratio 4.2$\times$, bar 3$\times$),
but the *velocity* leg's low-Re prediction was refuted — the linear
arm's velocity gap to the nonlinear arms is flat at $\approx 0.19$
from Re 10 to Re 300 instead of vanishing toward the Stokes limit.
Two readings, not yet discriminated: (a) Re 10 is simply not Stokes —
at unit drive speed the convective term is already order-one, so the
map's shape-nonlinearity in the drive is present across the whole
sampled band and only the *pressure* (whose convective part is
quadratic-dominant) shows the graded approach; (b) part of the
velocity gap is not the nonlinearity wall at all but a
representation/optimization deficit of the linear read-in on this
feature-rich solver-labeled family. Discriminating (a) from (b) needs
a genuinely Stokes-regime band (Re $\le 1$), which the solver
handles trivially — logged as the follow-up experiment rather than
argued away, and completed as iteration 37 (@sec-ns-lowre). The Transolver baseline's landing point (0.95 combined,
against the floor's 1.19 and the transformer arms' 0.23–0.44) is its
first measurement on a solver-labeled nonlinear suite at the shared
15-epoch protocol; no ordering was pre-registered, and the honest
caveat is that this budget may simply undertrain it — the number is
reported, not weaponized.

**What this iteration establishes, honestly.** The suite exists with a
measured label credential — that is the load-bearing deliverable. The
labels are two orders (velocity) and one order (pressure) below typical
model errors; the pressure floor is the binding one and is stated in
the manifest rather than assumed. The Re-dependent wall gives the
program its first *graded* structural measurement: where the parity
and superposition walls were binary, this one has a height profile
that tracks a physical dimensionless number, and the linear arm's gap
to the nonlinear arms is now a function you can plot rather than a
single 1.0.

**What it does not establish.** At the time of this iteration no
operator-fidelity block (strong-form momentum residual of the model's
own outputs) was emitted by the N-S driver — on the exact-label suites
that block came from autograd against closed-form scales, and porting
it to solver-labeled data was logged as deliberate future work.
Iteration 37 closed that gap (@sec-ns-lowre); the archived runs in
@tbl-ns-arms predate it and keep their em-dash. The suite is
2D, steady, and moderate-Re by construction; nothing here speaks to
turbulence models, and the eval_unseen_Re band (200, 300] stays inside
the solver's verified Newton envelope (grid-verified through Re 400) —
extrapolation beyond the *solver's* comfort zone would make label
quality the confound. Near-wall queries sit at distance 0.02–0.08 with
production meshes graded to $h_b \approx 0.006$ at the boundary; a
higher-Re suite would need boundary-layer-resolving meshes and a fresh
noise-floor measurement.

#### The completed P1 measurable: the Re $\le$ 1 band {#sec-ns-lowre}

The low-Reynolds band settles what the production catalog could not:
the linear read-in class is *not* what costs velocity accuracy in the
near-Stokes regime — a missing parity sector was. The production gap
curve had sat flat at $\approx 0.19$ across Re 10–300, but that band
never reached the Stokes regime the prediction was *about* — at unit
drive speed, Re 10 already has an order-one convective term. Iteration 37
closes this with a **supplementary catalog slice**,
`ns_cavity_star/v1-lowre`: 180 cases with train/eval_id at
$\mathrm{Re}$ log-uniform $[0.5, 5]$ and the unseen-Re band directly
above at $(5, 10]$, generated by the same incremental generator with
the Reynolds band as the *only* moved axis (`--reynolds-range`;
geometry, drive family, $h = 0.0105$, and the full verification
discipline are the production family's, with the measured label-noise
floors in the slice manifest). The linear and nonlinear arms retrain
on the slice at the identical 15-epoch/3-seed protocol, and their
per-case velocity gap joins the archived iteration-36 curve into one
measurement spanning Re 0.5–300. Iteration 38 then closed the one
confound iteration 37 logged inside its own verdict — its linear arm
differed from nl_pseudo in parity machinery and capacity as well as
read-in class — by adding the fair control
`mt_singpair_linear_pseudo` (linear read-in *plus* the nonlinear arm's
`drive_pseudo_dim=8` sector) on both catalogs and recomputing the
whole curve with three arms. Artifacts:
`results/ns_lowre_band_2026-07-05.json`, archive key
`iteration_37_lowre_band`;
`results/ns_linear_pseudo_confound_2026-07-05.json`, archive key
`iteration_38_linear_pseudo_confound`.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ns-lowre-gap
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The completed three-arm gap curve (iterations 37 + 38): each arm's
#|   gap to the nonlinear reference (arm minus nl_pseudo per-case mean
#|   per log-Re bin, eval_id + eval_unseen_Re pooled over 3 seeds)
#|   across Re 0.5-300, velocity left, pressure right. Filled circles:
#|   the v1-lowre slice (108-case train split); open squares: the
#|   production v1 catalog (840-case train split); each side is
#|   internally controlled, so the GAP crosses the seam (dashed) even
#|   though absolute errors do not. The plain linear arm (red)
#|   reproduces iteration 37: velocity gap flat at ~0.13-0.23
#|   everywhere, including the genuinely drive-linear band. The
#|   iteration-38 fair control (blue, the same linear read-in PLUS the
#|   nl arm's drive_pseudo_dim=8 sector) collapses the velocity gap to
#|   zero-or-negative across the entire near-Stokes band and leaves a
#|   graded remainder growing to ~0.10-0.12 by Re 100-213: the
#|   pre-registered REVISION outcome -- iteration 37's flat gap was the
#|   missing parity sector, not the linear read-in class. Both arms'
#|   pressure gaps collapse at low Re and grow to ~0.5: the pressure
#|   wall is physics, and no pseudo sector rescues a drive-linear
#|   read-in from a drive-nonlinear target.
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

confound = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" /
                          "ns_linear_pseudo_confound_2026-07-05.json"))
joined = confound["re_gap_curves"]["joined"]
seam = 10.0
arms = (
    ("mt_singpair_linear", "#e34948", "linear (no pseudo, 106k)"),
    ("mt_singpair_linear_pseudo", "#1a6feb", "linear + pseudo (131k)"),
)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.6, 3.8), sharex=True,
                         sharey=True)
for ax, field in zip(axes, ("velocity", "pressure")):
    low_edge = min(joined[arms[0][0]]["bin_centers"]) / 1.4
    ax.axvspan(low_edge, 1.0, color="#eceaf4", zorder=0)
    ax.axhline(0.0, color="#e1e0d9", lw=1.0, zorder=1)
    ax.axvline(seam, color="#a7a6a1", lw=1.0, ls="--", zorder=1)
    for arm, color, label in arms:
        entry = joined[arm]
        centers = np.array(entry["bin_centers"])
        values = np.array(entry[f"{field}_gap"])
        catalog = np.array(entry["catalog"])
        ax.plot(centers, values, "-", lw=1.3, color=color, label=label,
                zorder=2)
        for cat, marker, face in (("v1-lowre", "o", color),
                                  ("v1", "s", "white")):
            mask = catalog == cat
            ax.plot(centers[mask], values[mask], marker, ms=5, lw=0,
                    color=color, markerfacecolor=face,
                    markeredgecolor=color, zorder=3)
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_ylim(-0.12, 0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("case Reynolds number [-]")
    ax.set_title(f"{field} gap to nl_pseudo", fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8, which="both", axis="x")
    for spine in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
axes[0].set_ylabel("arm $-$ nl_pseudo relative $L^2$ gap [-]")
axes[0].text(0.72, -0.108, "near-Stokes\n(drive-linear)",
             fontsize=7.5, color="#52514e", ha="center", va="bottom")
axes[0].text(90.0, -0.108, "convection-dominated",
             fontsize=7.5, color="#52514e", ha="center", va="bottom")
axes[0].annotate("catalog join", (seam, 0.34),
                 xytext=(3, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                 fontsize=7, color="#52514e", rotation=90, va="bottom")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False, loc="upper left")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**Pre-registered versus measured, completed.** The rule (logged before
the first v1-lowre training run, @sec-nb-iter37): if the velocity map
is near-Stokes-linear at Re $\le 1$, the linear arm's velocity gap
approaches zero at the bottom joined bin (bar: $\le 0.05$ and
$\le 0.25\times$ the top bin) and grows monotonically; falsifier:
bottom-bin gap $\ge 0.1$ (the representation-deficit reading of the
iteration-36 anomaly). Measured: bottom-bin velocity gap **0.184**
against a top-bin 0.204 (ratio 1.10) — **the falsifier fired**. The
velocity leg of P1 is now refuted on a band where the physics cannot
be blamed: at Re $\le 1$ the map is near-Stokes — and the same
figure's pressure gap sitting at zero *proves the linear arm can match
the nonlinear arm on this band when the map is near-linear* — yet the
velocity gap stays at the same $\approx 0.18$ as at Re 300.
Reading (b) of the iteration-36 anomaly survived at that point — but
iteration 37's own verdict flagged the entanglement honestly: its
linear arm lacked the nonlinear arm's pseudo sector and carried
2.2$\times$ fewer parameters, so "linear read-in deficit" was
confounded with "parity/capacity deficit". The
**pressure** leg completes cleanly: its gap is zero within seed noise
across the whole near-Stokes band ($-0.006$, $+0.020$, $-0.042$ at
Re $< 5$ — the linear arm even wins two bins) and climbs to
0.47–0.54 at the top — the graded, physics-tracking wall the
pre-registration predicted, now measured from genuinely-Stokes to
convection-dominated.

**The confound check (iteration 38) — the revision fired.** The fair
control, `mt_singpair_linear_pseudo`: the identical linear field mode
(exact fixed-geometry drive superposition, structurally certified
odd-in-the-drive in-tree) *plus* `drive_pseudo_dim=8` — as matched to
nl_pseudo as the mode allows. Parameters: linear 106,408; linear +
pseudo **131,248**; nl_pseudo 233,108 — the pseudo sector adds 24,840
parameters, and the remaining difference to nl_pseudo *is* the
nonlinear read-in stack, i.e. exactly the treatment variable. Trained
on **both** catalogs (v1-lowre and v1) at the identical
15-epoch/3-seed protocol; pre-registered before the first run, both
outcomes stated in advance: bottom joined-bin velocity gap
$\le 0.05$ REVISES iteration 37 (the deficit was parity/capacity);
$\ge 0.1$ means the read-in-class reading stands, unconfounded.
Measured: bottom-bin velocity gap $\mathbf{-0.024}$ (the linear+pseudo
arm *beats* nl_pseudo on the Stokes band; the plain linear arm's
0.184 reproduces bin-for-bin in the same rerun) — **the revision
fired. Iteration 37's velocity reading is revised: the linear read-in
class is fine where the physics is linear; the flat gap was the
missing pseudo/parity sector, not the read-in.** And with the
confound removed, the velocity gap acquires the graded shape the
original P1 predicted all along: $\approx 0$ (to $-0.05$) across
Re 0.5–7, rising to 0.10–0.12 at Re 100–213 (@fig-ns-lowre-gap, left).
The pressure column sharpens the same story from the other side: the
pseudo sector does *nothing* for the pressure gap (0.016 at the
bottom bin, 0.45–0.54 at the top — bin-for-bin the plain linear
arm's curve), and on the production catalog nl_pseudo still wins
pressure decisively (0.356 vs 0.684 eval_id) — a drive-nonlinear
target stays out of reach of any drive-linear read-in, pseudo sector
or not. That asymmetry, now unconfounded, is the section's finding:
the graded Re-tracking wall is real for *both* fields — velocity's
was just an order of magnitude smaller than the parity artifact that
sat on top of it. One caveat stays on the record: linear+pseudo
matches nl_pseudo's sector structure, not its full width (131k vs
233k); a width-matched linear control was not run, so "capacity" and
"parity machinery" are separated from the read-in class but not from
each other.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ns-lowre
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path

confound = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" /
                          "ns_linear_pseudo_confound_2026-07-05.json"))
arms = confound["arms_lowre"]
order = ["mt_singpair_nl_pseudo", "mt_singpair_linear_pseudo",
         "mt_singpair_linear"]
labels = {
    "mt_singpair_nl_pseudo": "MT nonlinear + pseudo",
    "mt_singpair_linear_pseudo": "MT linear + pseudo (iter-38 control)",
    "mt_singpair_linear": "MT linear (wall control)",
}
splits = ["eval_id", "eval_unseen_Re", "eval_unseen_geometry",
          "eval_unseen_drive_profile"]
headers = (["arm", "params"] + [s.replace("eval_", "").replace("_", "-")
                                for s in splits]
           + ["momentum res. (ID)", "divergence res. (ID)"])
print("| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |")
print("|" + "---|" * len(headers))
for arm in order:
    row = [labels[arm], f"{arms[arm]['parameters']:,}"]
    for split in splits:
        cell = arms[arm]["splits"][split]["combined"]
        row.append(f"{cell['mean']:.3f} ± {cell['sd']:.3f}")
    for key in ("momentum_residual", "divergence_residual"):
        cell = arms[arm]["fidelity"][key]["eval_id"]
        row.append(f"{cell['mean']:.2f} ± {cell['sd']:.2f}")
    print("| " + " | ".join(row) + " |")
print()
n_train = confound["dataset"]["lowre_split_sizes"]["train"]
print(": The v1-lowre slice arms (combined relative $L^2$, mean ± sd "
f"over 3 seeds, {n_train}-case train split; iteration-37 arms plus "
"the iteration-38 confound control) with the suite's first populated "
"fidelity columns: the strong-form momentum residual "
"$\\|\\tilde\\nu\\Delta u - (u\\cdot\\nabla)u - \\nabla p\\| / "
"\\|(u\\cdot\\nabla)u\\|$ of the model's own prediction and the "
"matching divergence norm (float64 autograd, 32 interior queries, "
"2 cases/split; $\\tilde\\nu$ from the case -- the model never sees "
"the PDE, the metric does). {#tbl-ns-lowre}")
```

The fidelity block itself is the iteration's second deliverable — the
N-S port of the @sec-fidelity-columns convention to solver-labeled
data, where no closed-form scale exists: the residual is normalized by
the prediction's *own* advection norm, and the instrument is certified
in-tree before use — the exact Kovasznay solution scores $\sim 0$
*only* when the metric uses the case's $\tilde\nu$ (pinning the
"$\tilde\nu$ from the case" plumbing), and a rigid rotation with its
pressure dropped scores exactly 1
(`test_fidelity_residuals_certify_the_instrument`). As on every suite
since the column became first-class, the strong-form numbers are
diagnostics of *how* the arms fit, not who wins: they complement the
$L^2$ columns and cannot be gamed by a constant field, which zeroes
the interior strong form while failing the boundary conditions — the
note in the driver states this explicitly. Read the low-Re magnitudes
with the normalization in mind: near Stokes the true advection is
small while $\tilde\nu$ is order one, so the advection-normalized
residual amplifies second-derivative model error by
$\sim \tilde\nu/\|(u\cdot\nabla)u\|$ — the O(10) values in
@tbl-ns-lowre say the predictions' derivatives do not satisfy the
operator (consistent with every suite since @sec-fidelity-columns:
$L^2$-fit fields, unsatisfied operators). The three-arm ordering
tracks the velocity story exactly: the plain linear arm's momentum
residual (47.7) and divergence norm (2.70) sit 2–3$\times$ above the
other two, while the iteration-38 linear+pseudo control lands beside
nl_pseudo (momentum 22.2 vs 16.1) and *beats* it on divergence (0.85
vs 1.07) — the fidelity instrument independently confirms that the
pseudo sector, not the nonlinear read-in, is what the plain linear
arm's velocity was missing.
